limitations: Owners must select approved type/status/title, safe detail and disclosure of optional resource/version/blocker references. String validation does not prove content contains no sensitive material.
Retryability is an opaque owner classification, not permission to retry. Unknown external outcomes require owning-domain reconciliation.

Create returns a caller-owned mutable framework body; HttpResult owns an independent private snapshot. Consumers receive representation only; HTTP response status remains authoritative for generic HTTP handling.
No public endpoint or SDK is published. Endpoint owners must explicitly declare ProblemDetails response metadata in OpenAPI when activating the capability.
Reviews are Codex engineering reviews, not independent human, Product or production acceptance.
ownership_note: The P1-017 decomposition row is shared coordination metadata. Only new Problem Details source/tests/guide are owned behavior; historical command primitives and OpenAPI composition were not edited. Later evidence/context/closure edits are metadata and are separately committed before completion.
acceptance_results: Current canonical Document 32 section 6 resolves the omitted-contract finding; Documents 07/05 establish API/SDK compatibility without new authority.
Framework ProblemDetails and existing TechnicalProblemCodes are reused; the thirteen canonical classes are recognizable and future approved strings are preserved.
HTTP result uses a private snapshot with matching body/HTTP status and canonical application/problem+json; optional safe metadata is omitted rather than inferred.
RFC-compatible reading ignores wrong-typed standard members, preserves future extensions as document-independent clones and performs no URI lookup, detail-based classification or retry execution.
No new endpoint, exception middleware, SDK package, domain taxonomy or status/retry policy is implemented. Historical prerequisite evidence and command/host/OpenAPI behavior remain preserved.
